acid-reflux: When acid from your stomach rises back up into your food pipe.
amh: A hormone made by the small follicles in your ovaries that hold developing eggs.
amino-acids: The small building blocks that join together to make proteins.
anaemia: Your blood has fewer red blood cells than normal, or less haemoglobin inside them.
anti-tpo: Proteins made by your own immune system that attack thyroid peroxidase, an enzyme your thyroid needs to make its hormones.
antioxidants: Natural or man-made substances that may prevent or delay some kinds of damage to your cells.
bloating: When your tummy feels full, tight and uncomfortable, and it may look swollen too.
bmi: A number worked out from your weight and height: your weight in kilograms divided by your height in metres, squared.
bmr: The minimum number of calories your body needs just to keep going at complete rest: to breathe, keep your heart beating, circulate blood and hold your body…
body-fat-percentage: The share of your total body weight that is fat, rather than muscle, bone, water and organs.
calcium: A mineral your body uses to build bones and teeth, where almost all of it is stored.
calorie-deficit: Eating and drinking fewer calories than your body uses.
calorie: A unit that measures the energy in food and drink.
carbohydrate: One of the three main nutrients in food.
chaas: Indian buttermilk: dahi whisked with plenty of water and usually seasoned with roasted jeera, salt, mint, ginger or curry leaves.
complete-protein: A food protein that contains all the essential amino acids, the building blocks your body cannot make itself, in the right proportions.
constipation: You're passing stool less often than usual, often fewer than three times a week, or that it's hard, dry, lumpy or painful to pass.
cortisol: A hormone made by your adrenal glands, often called the stress hormone.
crash-diet: Any plan that cuts your food so drastically that you lose weight very quickly, often more than a kilo a week.
cravings: A craving is a strong, specific urge for a particular food, very often something sweet, salty or fried, that feels different from ordinary hunger.
creatinine: A normal waste product made when your muscles work and some muscle tissue breaks down.
crp: A protein your liver makes when there is inflammation in your body.
dexa-scan: A quick, low-dose X-ray that measures how much calcium and other minerals are packed into your bones.
dhea-s: A hormone made mostly by your adrenal glands, two small glands that sit on top of your kidneys.
dietary-fat: The fat in the food you eat, from oils, ghee and butter to nuts, seeds, milk, meat and fish.
electrolytes: Minerals that carry a tiny electrical charge when they dissolve in your body fluids.
emotional-eating: Eating to soothe, numb or change a feeling, like stress, boredom, loneliness or sadness, rather than because your body is physically hungry.
fasting-blood-sugar: The amount of glucose in your blood after you have not eaten anything, usually overnight.
fasting-insulin: The amount of insulin in your blood after an overnight fast.
fatty-liver: When too much fat builds up in your liver.
fermented-foods: Foods in which friendly bacteria or yeast have broken down some of the sugars and starches.
ferritin: A protein that stores iron inside your body.
fibre: The part of plant foods that your body can't fully digest.
fsh: A hormone made by the pituitary gland in your brain.
gestational-diabetes: Diabetes that appears for the first time during pregnancy.
glucose: The main sugar in your blood and your body's main source of energy.
gluten: A protein found naturally in wheat, barley and rye.
glycemic-index: A score from 0 to 100 that shows how quickly a food containing carbohydrate raises your blood sugar.
glycemic-load: A score that looks at both how quickly a food raises your blood sugar (its glycemic index) and how much carbohydrate is in the portion you actually eat.
haemoglobin: The iron-rich protein inside your red blood cells that carries oxygen from your lungs to the rest of your body.
hashimotos: An autoimmune condition where your immune system mistakenly attacks your thyroid gland.
hba1c: A blood test that shows your average blood sugar over the past two to three months.
homa-ir: A number worked out from two fasting blood tests, your fasting glucose and your fasting insulin.
hot-flashes: A sudden wave of heat over your face, neck and chest, often with sweating and red, flushed skin.
hydration: Having enough water in your body to keep it working properly.
hyperthyroidism: When your thyroid gland makes more hormone than your body needs.
hypothyroidism: When the thyroid gland in your neck doesn't make enough thyroid hormone.
ibs: A common, usually long-term condition of the digestive system.
icmr-nin: The National Institute of Nutrition in Hyderabad, part of the Indian Council of Medical Research.
ideal-body-weight: An estimate of the weight that suits your height.
idli: A soft, steamed cake made from a fermented batter of rice and urad dal.
ifct: The Indian Food Composition Tables, a large reference of what's inside Indian foods.
insoluble-fibre: The type of fibre that doesn't dissolve in water.
insulin-resistance: When your muscles, fat and liver don't respond well to insulin, the hormone that moves sugar from your blood into your cells.
insulin: A hormone made by your pancreas.
intermittent-fasting: An eating pattern that switches between set periods of eating and not eating.
iron-deficiency: Your body doesn't have enough iron.
iron: A mineral your body uses to make haemoglobin, the part of your red blood cells that carries oxygen around your body.
kalonji: Tiny, matt black, teardrop-shaped seeds with a mildly bitter, onion-like taste.
katori: The small steel or ceramic bowl that sits on an Indian thali, used to serve dal, sabzi, dahi or kheer.
khichdi: Rice and dal cooked together into a soft, one-pot meal, usually with haldi, a little ghee and a jeera tadka.
kuttu: Buckwheat, and kuttu ka atta is the flour made from its seeds.
lactose-intolerance: Your gut doesn't make enough lactase, the enzyme that breaks down lactose, the natural sugar in milk.
lassi: A thick drink made by churning dahi with water or milk.
lh-fsh-ratio: The LH:FSH ratio compares two hormones from your brain that control your ovaries, luteinising hormone and follicle stimulating hormone.
lh: A hormone made by the pituitary gland in your brain.
macronutrients: The three nutrients your body needs in large amounts: carbohydrates, protein and fat.
magnesium: A mineral your body uses in more than 300 chemical reactions.
makhana: The popped seed of Euryale ferox, a prickly water lily that grows in still ponds, mostly in Bihar.
masala-dabba: The round steel spice box found in most Indian kitchens, with small bowls inside for everyday spices such as haldi, jeera, rai, dhania powder, lal mirch, garam…
meal-timing: When you eat through the day, how far apart your meals are and how regular they are from one day to the next.
menopause: When your periods stop for good because your hormone levels have fallen.
metabolism: All the chemical work your body does to turn food and drink into energy.
methi-water: Made by soaking fenugreek seeds in water overnight and drinking the water, sometimes with the softened seeds, in the morning.
micronutrients: The vitamins and minerals your body needs in very small amounts, such as iron, iodine, folate, vitamin A, vitamin B12, vitamin D and calcium.
millets: Small-seeded grains that have been part of Indian kitchens for centuries.
mindful-eating: Slowing down and paying full attention to your food and your body while you eat.
oestrogen: A group of female sex hormones made mainly by the ovaries.
ogtt: The oral glucose tolerance test checks how your body handles a large dose of sugar.
omega-3: A family of healthy fats found in food and in your body.
osteopenia: Your bones are less dense than they should be, but not yet thin enough to be called osteoporosis.
osteoporosis: A condition where your bones lose density and strength and become fragile, so they break much more easily.
oxalate: A natural compound found in many plant foods, such as spinach, nuts, peanuts, wheat bran and rhubarb.
pcod: A name widely used in India for the hormone condition that doctors elsewhere call PCOS.
pcos: A common hormone condition in women that can affect periods, fertility, skin, hair, weight and mood.
perimenopause: The transition years before menopause, when your ovaries gradually make less oestrogen and your periods start to change.
phytate: The natural form in which seeds store phosphorus.
phytoestrogens: Natural plant compounds that act a little like oestrogen, the hormone your body makes.
plateau: A stretch of weeks when the scale stops moving even though you're still following your diet and exercise plan.
portion-size: The amount of food you actually put on your plate and eat at one time.
postmenopause: The stage of life that starts once you've gone a full year without a period, and it lasts for the rest of your life.
postpartum-weight: The extra weight you carry after having a baby.
postprandial-blood-sugar: Your blood glucose measured after a meal, usually about two hours after you start eating.
potassium: A mineral and electrolyte that your heart, muscles and nerves need to work properly.
prebiotics: Types of carbohydrate, mostly fibre, that your body can't digest.
prediabetes: Your blood sugar is higher than normal but not yet high enough to be called diabetes.
probiotics: Live microorganisms, mostly friendly bacteria and some yeasts, that are meant to benefit your health when you eat them.
progesterone: A hormone made mainly by the ovaries after an egg is released each month.
prolactin: A hormone made by the pituitary gland, a pea-sized gland at the base of your brain.
protein: A nutrient your body uses to build and repair cells, from muscle and skin to hair.
pulses: The dried seeds of legume plants: the dals, beans and grams in your kitchen.
refined-carbohydrates: Grains and sugars that have been processed until most of their fibre, vitamins and minerals are gone.
sarcopenia: The gradual loss of muscle size, strength and function that comes with age.
satiety: The feeling of being comfortably full and satisfied after eating, the signal that tells you to stop and keeps you from feeling hungry again too soon.
sattu: A flour made by dry-roasting and grinding Bengal gram (chana), sometimes mixed with roasted barley or other grains.
saturated-fat: A type of fat that's usually solid at room temperature.
saunf: The seed of the fennel plant: small, greenish and slightly sweet, with an aniseed taste.
sgpt-alt: An enzyme found mostly in your liver.
shbg: A protein made mostly by your liver.
singhara: Flour made from dried singhara, the horned fruit of the water caltrop (Trapa), a plant that grows in ponds and lakes and is often called water chestnut in India.
sodium: A mineral and one of your body's main electrolytes.
soluble-fibre: The type of fibre that absorbs water and forms a soft gel in your gut during digestion.
t-score: The main number on a bone density (DEXA) report.
t3: One of the two main hormones your thyroid gland makes.
t4: The main hormone made by your thyroid gland in the front of your neck.
tadka: The step where whole spices like jeera, rai, hing, curry leaves or dried chillies are crackled in hot oil or ghee and poured over dal, sabzi or raita.
tdee: The total number of calories your body burns in a whole day.
testosterone: A hormone that both men and women make, though women make much smaller amounts.
thali: A complete Indian meal served on one large plate, with roti or rice at the centre and small katoris of dal, sabzi, dahi, salad and sometimes a sweet around it.
thermic-effect-of-food: The extra energy your body uses to digest, absorb and store the food you've just eaten.
total-cholesterol: The total amount of cholesterol in your blood, including both LDL (bad) and HDL (good) cholesterol.
triglycerides: A type of fat in your blood.
triphala: A traditional Ayurvedic mix of three dried fruits: amla, haritaki and bibhitaki, usually sold as a powder or tablets.
tsh: A hormone made by the pituitary gland in your brain.
type-2-diabetes: A long-term condition where your blood sugar stays too high because your body doesn't make enough insulin or can't use it well.
upma: A savoury South Indian breakfast made by roasting suji (semolina) and cooking it with water, vegetables and a tadka of mustard seeds, curry leaves and green…
uric-acid: A normal waste product your body makes when it breaks down purines, natural substances found in your own cells and in some foods and drinks.
visceral-fat: The fat stored deep inside your belly, packed around organs such as your liver, heart, kidneys and intestines.
vitamin-b12: A vitamin your body needs to make healthy red blood cells and keep your nerves working.
vitamin-c: A vitamin your body uses to grow and repair tissues.
vitamin-d: A vitamin your skin makes when it is exposed to sunlight, and you get a little from food.
waist-to-height-ratio: Your waist measurement divided by your height, using the same unit for both.
waist-to-hip-ratio: Your waist measurement divided by your hip measurement.
water-weight: The extra fluid your body holds on to at any given time.
whole-grains: A whole grain still has the entire grain kernel, including the outer bran and the germ.
yo-yo-dieting: The pattern of losing weight on a strict diet, putting it back on, and then dieting again, over and over.
zinc: A trace mineral, which means you need only small amounts, but it's found in cells all through your body.
